text: Then Jacob called for his sons and said: "Gather around, and I will tell you what will happen to you in the days to come.
Assemble and listen, sons of Jacob; listen to Israel your father.
Reuben, you are my firstborn, my might, the first fruit of my strength, excelling in honor, excelling in power.
Unruly as water, you will excel no longer, for you climbed onto your father's bed, onto my couch, and defiled it.
Simeon and Levi are brothers; their swords are weapons of violence.
Let me never enter their council, never join their assembly, for in their anger they killed men, and on a whim they crippled oxen.
Cursed be their anger, so fierce, and their fury, so cruel. I will divide them in Jacob and scatter them in Israel.
Judah, your brothers will praise you; your hand will be on the neck of your enemies; your father's sons will bow down before you.
Judah is a lion's cub; from the prey, my son, you have gone up. He crouches, he lies down like a lion, like a lioness—who dares rouse him?

until he comes to whom it belongs, and the obedience of the nations is his.[^1]

[^1]: Hebrew Shiloh; the meaning of the word is uncertain.

versions.text: The scepter will not depart from Judah, nor the ruler's staff from between his feet, until he comes to whom it belongs, and the obedience of the nations is his.
versions.explanation: The rendering interprets the difficult word Shiloh; a brief footnote alerts the reader that the Hebrew term is uncertain and is elsewhere transliterated.

text: He tethers his donkey to the vine, his colt to the choicest branch; he washes his garments in wine, his robes in the blood of grapes.
His eyes are darker than wine, his teeth whiter than milk.
Zebulun will dwell by the shore of the sea; he will be a haven for ships, and his border will reach to Sidon.
Issachar is a strong-boned donkey, lying down between the saddlebags.
He saw that his resting place was good and that the land was pleasant, so he bent his shoulder to the load and became a slave at forced labor.
Dan will judge his people as one of the tribes of Israel.
Dan will be a serpent by the road, a viper along the path, that bites the horse's heels so that its rider falls backward.
I wait for your salvation, LORD.
Gad will be raided by raiders, but he will raid at their heels.
Asher's food will be rich; he will provide delicacies fit for a king.

Naphtali is a doe set free that bears beautiful fawns.[^1]

[^1]: Or "who speaks beautiful words."

versions.text: Naphtali is a doe set free that bears beautiful fawns.
versions.explanation: The received Hebrew literally reads "who gives beautiful words"; "bears beautiful fawns" rests on a re-vocalization. A footnote preserves the traditional reading for the listener without changing the poetic line.

text: Joseph is a fruitful vine, a fruitful vine beside a spring, whose branches climb over the wall.
Archers attacked him bitterly; they shot at him and harassed him.

versions.text: With bitterness archers attacked him; they shot at him with hostility.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has three verbs: they embittered him, they shot, and they harbored hostility toward him. The current rendering collapses the last two into one phrase and loses the sense of sustained hatred (שׂטם). The revision keeps all three actions and reads more naturally aloud.

text: But his bow remained steady, and his arms stayed strong and nimble, from the hands of the Mighty One of Jacob—from there comes the Shepherd, the Rock of Israel—

versions.text: But his bow remained steady, and his arms stayed strong and nimble, by the hands of the Mighty One of Jacob, by the name of the Shepherd, the Rock of Israel,
versions.explanation: The Hebrew reads מִשָּׁם, "from there," not מִשֵּׁם, "from the name." The current wording follows a conjectural emendation without indication; the received text should be represented.

versions.text: But his bow remained steady, and his arms stayed strong and nimble, by the hands of the Mighty One of Jacob—from there comes the Shepherd, the Rock of Israel—
versions.explanation: מִידֵי is "from the hands of," marking the source of the strength; "by the hands" reads as agency of action rather than origin, and "from" also parallels the following מִשָּׁם ("from there"), tightening the rhythm of the couplet for oral reading.

text: by the God of your father, who helps you, by the Almighty, who blesses you with blessings of the heavens above, blessings of the deep that lies below, blessings of the breasts and the womb.

The blessings of your father are greater than the blessings of my forebears, reaching to the bounty of the everlasting hills. May they crown the head of Joseph, the brow of him who was set apart among his brothers.

versions.text: The blessings of your father are greater than the blessings of the ancient mountains, than the bounty of the everlasting hills. Let them rest on the head of Joseph, on the brow of the prince among his brothers.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew הוֹרַי means "my progenitors/forebears"; "the ancient mountains" reflects a conjectural emendation. A footnote could note the alternative reading "the ancient mountains."

versions.text: The blessings of your father are greater than the blessings of my forebears, reaching to the bounty of the everlasting hills.
versions.explanation: The final clause of the Hebrew verse (תִּהְיֶין לְרֹאשׁ יוֹסֵף וּלְקָדְקֹד נְזִיר אֶחָיו) has been dropped entirely, leaving the blessing without its recipient and breaking the flow into verse 27. The restored clause renders נְזִיר as 'set apart' rather than 'prince', reflecting the root meaning of consecration/separation.

versions.text: The blessings of your father are greater than the blessings of my forebears, reaching to the bounty of the everlasting hills. May they crown the head of Joseph, the brow of him who was set apart from his brothers.
versions.explanation: נְזִיר אֶחָיו denotes the one consecrated/distinguished within the family circle, not one separated away from his brothers. "From his brothers" suggests estrangement or exclusion, which reverses the sense of honor intended; "among his brothers" preserves both the consecration nuance retained in the previous revision and the correct relational sense.

text: Benjamin is a ravenous wolf; in the morning he devours the prey, in the evening he divides the spoil."
All these are the twelve tribes of Israel, and this is what their father said to them when he blessed them, giving each the blessing that belonged to him.
Then he gave them these instructions: "I am about to be gathered to my people. Bury me with my fathers in the cave in the field of Ephron the Hittite,
the cave in the field of Machpelah, near Mamre in the land of Canaan, the field Abraham bought from Ephron the Hittite as a burial site.
There Abraham and his wife Sarah were buried; there Isaac and his wife Rebekah were buried; and there I buried Leah.
The field and the cave in it were bought from the Hittites."
When Jacob had finished giving instructions to his sons, he drew his feet up into the bed, breathed his last, and was gathered to his people.
